messages:
maya: Heads-up — LegalCorp wants a commercial SLA: 99.9% uptime + p99 latency guarantee for hosted API (seq128) and an option for Dedicated with contractual isolation. We need to map to pricing tiers and readiness checklist.

sam: Do we have an internal cost estimate for maintaining p99 targets vs. standard offering? Basic numbers will drive pricing uplift.

kevin: Finance quick take: roughs — +15-25% for a 99.5% SLA, +25-45% for 99.9% (depends on dedicated vs shared). Need eng latency/cost inputs before finalizing.

carmen: Important: customer is pushing for explicit response-time SLOs (p99) not just uptime credits. That changes what runbooks and monitoring we must promise.

oliver: For seq128 on our current serving configs: p99 on Hosted (mixed tenants) sits ~200-350ms depending on batching and cache hit. Dedicated with tuned batching + prefix cache: ~160-220ms. I can produce a bench matrix across seq64/128/512.

lena: Docs side: committing SLA means we must ship: 1) SLO dashboard per-customer, 2) runbook with alerting thresholds and escalation path, 3) public SLA doc + internal incident playbook. Who owns these?

maya: I'll own the SLA doc wording + customer comms. @lena you own runbooks/docs. Need to decide on alert thresholds and oncall routing.

sam: Proposed routing: Tier1 support (CS) -> Tier2 infra (eng-infra) -> eng-runtime oncall. We also need a fast path for Enterprise SLA customers to reach an escalation engineer.

oncall-bot: ALERT TEMPLATE: SLA-BREACH-CUSTOMER (trigger if p99_latency > 300ms for 5m OR error_rate > 0.5%) -> page: eng-runtime-escalation.

kevin: Commercial proposal: three bundles: Standard (no SLA), Business (+SLA 99.5%, shared infra), Enterprise (+SLA 99.9%, option for Dedicated, priority support). I'll draft uplift ranges and contract bullets.

carmen: Add canary fallback policy to the readiness list — if primary model variant exceeds p99 threshold, automatic fallback to lower-quality but faster variant until fixed. Must be in runbook.

oliver: Action: I'll run systematic benchmarks and recommend batching/cache knobs. Deliverable: CSV with p50/p95/p99 and cost-per-token estimates for seq64/128/512 by Tue.

lena: Action: I'll draft the runbook + escalation matrix and SLO dashboard spec by Wed EOD. Need a sample legal clause for SLA credits — @kevin can you loop in legal?

kevin: Will loop legal and sketch contract language. Example snippet for discussion: `SLA: 99.9% availability measured monthly; p99 latency <= 250ms for seq128; service credits of 10% for monthly availability <99.9%`. Open to engineering changes.

maya: Launch readiness checklist (high level):
- SLA contract language agreed with legal and finance
- Runbook + escalation matrix published
- SLO dashboards + alerting in observability
- Billing integration and pricing uplift assigned
- Dedicated provisioning playbook for Enterprise
- Canary fallback policy + docs

Anything missing?

carmen: Add acceptance test: simulated load test to validate SLOs end-to-end (inc. cache warmup behavior).

oliver: Noted, will include in bench plan.

maya: Owners recap: oliver (benchmarks/acceptance tests), lena (runbook/docs/dashboards), kevin (pricing + legal liaison), sam (oncall routing + escalation), carmen (SLA policy + fallback). I'll schedule a 30m sync Thu 11am PT to finalize. React :thumbsup: if you can make it.

sam: :thumbsup:

carmen: :thumbsup:, pinged legal.

maya: Doc placeholder: https://redwood.company/ops/sla-proposals/legalcorp-draft (internal) — will update after benchmarks.

kevin: I'll attach initial pricing ranges in that doc before the sync.

lena: I'll drop a runbook stub in docs and link alerts.

maya: Thanks all — let's keep this tight, customer wants decision window next week.
